findings.rule: robustness against hostile input / performance: every regex of the module must be linear (module docstring lines 6-7)
findings.evidence: _COMMENT = r'<!--.*?-->' is applied with .sub() to every line in unfenced() (line 93), and unfenced() runs for plan.md (validate, goal render, ship) and implementation.md (goal render, ship). A line with many '<!--' and no '-->' is quadratic: each opening scans lazily to the end of the line. Measured with evidence_class_errors on '<!--' repeated: 16 KB 0.18 s, 32 KB 0.74 s, 64 KB 3.0 s, 128 KB 13.0 s, 256 KB over the 20 s alarm. recorded_release_rows gives the same timings for a proof row. Every other pattern is linear: 25 other plan shapes and 6 other implementation shapes stay under 0.2 s at 256 KB, including the r2 heading case. Not blocking: it needs a crafted line of more than about 100 KB, where the r2 defect hung on 4 KB.
findings.correction: Remove the regex and scan with str.find: loop on start = line.find('<!--', pos), end = line.find('-->', start + 4), drop the text between them, and if end is -1 keep line[:start] and set comment=True. Add '<!--' * 50_000 to the time-bounded test at tests/test_plan_evidence_class.py:74.

findings.rule: AC-003 / fail-safe: the parser and the Markdown renderer must agree on what is hidden
findings.evidence: Three shapes hide a visible declaration from the parser, so the step stays local and require_progression(..., 'ship') returns READY with no proof (probe_ship.py). (1) Inline code '`<!--`' with no '-->' on the line opens a comment (line 94), and every later line is dropped until some '-->'. That includes later Step headings and declarations. CommonMark does not open a comment inside a code span, so this one can happen by accident in a plan about HTML anchors (no current repo plan has it). (2) Text after '-->' on the closing line of a multi-line comment is dropped (line 88): '<!-- note' then '--> **Evidence class:** release'. (3) A line '```a`' opens a fence for _FENCE, but CommonMark does not, because a backtick info string may not contain a backtick. A following '**Evidence class:** release' is rendered but skipped, and '```b`' closes the fence because _FENCE ignores trailing text. Shapes (2) and (3) are deliberate, visible tricks.
findings.correction: Drop code spans (_INLINE_CODE) before looking for '<!--'. On a closing line, keep the text after '-->' and process it. Treat a backtick fence whose info string contains a backtick as text, and accept a closing fence only when nothing but spaces follows it. Add a regression case for each shape to test_invalid_evidence_classes_are_reported.

findings.rule: robustness: a fictitious release proof satisfies /spec-ship (r1/r2 placeholder finding, further narrowed)
findings.evidence: Closed since r2: '?', 'TBC', 'will be signed later', '_pending_', '[ ]', 'no proof yet', 'blocked', 'x', 'false', '<receipt>' and the construction emoji are now refused. Because only the first mark or word is checked, these still count as proof and ship returns READY: 'Proof pending', 'Notary receipt pending', '**Status:** TBD', '<pending>', '...', '✅', '✓', 'ok', 'yes', 'done'. execution-rules.md says a proof cell must not just announce a proof, but these announce one or name nothing.
findings.correction: Require the proof cell to contain something checkable: a path or file name with an extension, a URL, or an identifier with a digit. Alternatively, also refuse a cell in which any word is one of the _NOT_A_PROOF_WORDS (not only the first word), and refuse cells with no letter or digit. Document the rule in execution-rules.md.

findings.evidence: _ANY_CLASS ('[eé]vidence[ \t]+class[*_ \t]*:') misses some rendered-equivalent forms. These are not flagged, the step stays local and ship returns READY: 'Evidence class: release', '**Evidence class:** release' (no-break space), '**Evidence-class:** release' and 'Evidence class — release'. Closed since r2: whole-bold, plain, single-star, double-space and accented forms now give release_evidence_invalid.
findings.correction: Widen the separators to [\s -]+ and allow '</?\w+>' between 'class' and ':', or flag any unfenced line where 'evidence' and 'class' are adjacent words, whatever comes after them.

findings.evidence: normalize_label calls int() on each component. With Python 3.14's limit of 4300 digits for integer string conversion, a step number or proof label longer than 4300 digits raises ValueError. That ValueError escapes evidence_class_errors: `livespec validate plan.md` exits 1 with a traceback, release_goal_context crashes (it catches only OSError) and require_progression raises a bare ValueError. The ship gate still fails closed.

The heading match is _key(title) == 'release evidence' at any depth and in any case, so '#### release evidence' opens the proof table. execution-rules.md and the module docstring say 'a heading exactly `## Release Evidence`'. Harmless, because the text must still be exactly Release Evidence. A 4-cell row ('| 1 | Sign | r.json | extra |') is accepted and the extra cell ignored.
findings.correction: Either check depth 2 or reword the docs to 'a heading whose text is Release Evidence'.
